LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION- HOMONYMS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you distinguish the meaning between two different words with the same spelling?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate writing in indigenous languages for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 6.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION- HOMONYMS
This lesson teaches Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms for Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. appreciate writing in indigenous languages for enjoyment
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms above.
2. Explain Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 6.3.1 Writing for information- Homonyms important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you distinguish the meaning between two different words with the same spelling?
2. Why do economic activities differ from one location to another?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. appreciate writing in indigenous languages for enjoyment

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
